F1.question: What the district did, or failed to do
F1.answer: the IEP of August 21, 2025 requires 60 minutes per week of individual speech-language therapy; from the week of September 22, 2025 the district delivered 30 minutes per week in a group of three, with no service in three weeks, for a total of 690 minutes against 1,320 required through January 30, 2026, and did not amend the IEP; the parent requested an independent educational evaluation in writing on November 10, 2025 and the district refused it on December 4, 2025 without filing for a hearing; the district's May 6, 2025 evaluation did not assess written expression.

F2.question: How the client learned of it
F2.answer: from the service log the district sent on January 21, 2026, from the prior written notice of December 4, 2025, and from the student's own reports.

F3.question: Effect on the student
F3.answer: her expressive language remains at the 2nd percentile per the May 2025 CELF-5 and she has become reluctant to speak in class, per the IEP's present levels.

F4.question: Relief sought
F4.answer: compensatory speech-language therapy, delivered individually, equal to the minutes not delivered from September 22, 2025 to the date of the order; an independent educational evaluation in speech-language and written expression at public expense; and restoration of individual speech-language therapy at 60 minutes per week as the IEP requires.

events.what: the District’s speech-language pathologist administered the CELF-5 to Student; the evaluation is dated May 6, 2025.

the IEP team met for Student’s annual review; the IEP provides speech-language therapy at 60 minutes per week, individual, from August 21, 2025 to August 20, 2026; the team declined the Parent’s request to reevaluate written expression; and the Parent signed, writing that she still wanted written expression tested.
individual speech-language sessions ended when the provider’s caseload was reassigned; the log records 30 minutes in a group of 3 for that week.
the log records no speech-language service for the week (provider absent; no make-up scheduled).
The Parent requested in writing an independent educational evaluation in speech-language and written expression at public expense, stating disagreement with the evaluation of May 6, 2025.
the log records no speech-language service for the week (holiday week).

the District issued a prior written notice declining to fund an independent educational evaluation, stating that it considers the May 6, 2025 evaluation appropriate and will assess written expression in the spring 2026 reevaluation window.
The Parent wrote to the District that Student reported her speech sessions were with two other students and half as long, and asked for the service log and when individual sessions would resume.
the log records no speech-language service for the week (provider absent; no make-up scheduled).

The District sent the speech-language service log and wrote that the provider's caseload was reassigned in September and individual sessions have not been available since; it expects to post a second SLP position this spring.

the service log period ended; its summary states 22 weeks, 4 at 60 minutes individual, 15 at 30 minutes group, 3 with no service, and 690 total minutes delivered against 1,320 required by the IEP for 22 weeks.

The Parent wrote that the log shows 690 minutes delivered against 1,320 required, asked the District to make up the missed minutes and restore individual sessions now, and noted no response about the independent evaluation beyond the December 4 notice.
